articleHeadlineTranslated: Can blowing on cooled food spread hand, foot, and mouth disease to children?
articleHeadline: Thổi nguội thức ăn có lây bệnh tay chân miệng cho trẻ không?
articleSummary: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease (HFMD) is caused by Enteroviruses, especially EV71 and Coxsackieviruses A16 and A6. In Hanoi, Vietnam, transmission occurs via direct contact with feces or saliva and via droplets from the upper respiratory tract. Blowing on cooled food can spread HFMD to children, as droplets from saliva may contaminate food when adults feel well. The virus can survive on surfaces and food for hours, making contaminated food a transmission source. Safer cooling methods include natural cooling at room temperature, placing bowls in a basin of cool water, or stirring to dissipate heat. Other risks include kissing, sharing utensils, not washing hands before feeding, after diaper changes, or touching a child’s face with dirty hands. Stopping this habit may also reduce risks of CMV, hepatitis A, seasonal influenza, and Helicobacter pylori. Virus shedding in stool can persist for up to a month after symptoms end. Source: ThS.BS Le Thi Lan Anh, Hanoi.

articleHeadlineTranslated: Tuberculosis still poses a challenge to early diagnosis in Brazil.
articleHeadline: Tuberculose ainda desafia diagnóstico precoce no Brasil
articleSummary: Brazil reports ~85,000 new tuberculosis cases in 2024, about 10 diagnoses per hour, underscoring ongoing challenges in early detection. TB, caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, primarily targets the lungs but can involve lymph nodes, bones, or the central nervous system. Transmission is airborne via coughs, talks, or sneezes, with higher risk in closed, crowded, poorly ventilated spaces and prolonged contact. Early symptoms—cough lasting more than 2–3 weeks, fatigue, low-grade fever in the evening, night sweats, and unexplained weight loss—are often ignored, delaying care. Diagnosis via Brazil’s public health system (SUS) uses sputum analysis, rapid molecular tests, and chest radiography, enabling same-day treatment initiation. Treatment lasts at least six months and requires strict adherence to antibiotics to prevent relapse and resistance and to avoid permanent lung damage. Vaccination with BCG remains the principal protection against severe TB forms, alongside sustained routine immunization.

articleHeadline: Gene-Drive mosquito technology offers new hope in Africa's fight against malaria   - Ghana Business News
articleSummary: Gene-Drive technology to suppress malaria-carrying mosquitoes is being explored by Target Malaria (based at Imperial College London) across Africa, including Ghana and Nigeria. The approach aims to sterilize female mosquitoes by modifying genes controlling reproduction, spreading the modification through populations via gene-drive to near-100% inheritance rather than 50%. In cage studies (~600 mosquitoes), the modification spread rapidly and reproduction declined, with populations collapsing after several generations. Africa hosts more than 700 mosquito species, but only a subset (notably the Anopheles gambiae complex) drives most malaria transmission; the gene-drive targets malaria vectors while limiting broader ecological impact. Ghanaian sites conduct environmental and entomological studies; policymakers, communities, and stakeholders are engaged. No releases have occurred yet; extensive regulatory approvals, environmental assessments, and public consultations are required. If successful, this could complement bed nets, insecticides, and antimalarial meds, reducing transmission as populations fall.

articleSummary: Chikungunya remains highly active in Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, with the state recording over 3,600 probable cases and an incidence exceeding 200 cases per 100,000 residents across 14 municipalities. Seven deaths have been attributed to chikungunya this year, including an elderly woman in Jardim and a man aged 72 in Bonito; earlier fatalities occurred in Dourados and Dois Irmãos do Buriti in 2025. A cold front arriving from April 7–9 is forecast to lower temperatures to 12°C in the interior and 12–14°C by April 10–12, a trend that infectious disease experts say could slow Aedes aegypti transmission and viral spread. The ministry of health urges vector-control measures: eliminate standing water, properly dispose of containers, cover water tanks, and maintain clean gutters and water-storage facilities. Arbovirus seasonality in MS typically runs January–April, with case numbers easing from April into May.

articleSummary: Russia faces a severe animal-health crisis as authorities in multiple regions culled and incinerated thousands of cattle amid a suspected foot-and-mouth disease outbreak. In Siberian villages, mass slaughter left communities without livelihoods and with inadequate compensation; several areas placed under quarantine. Journalists documenting events were arrested, and Novosibirsk authorities publicly claimed a Pasteurella mutation to justify culling. The outbreak has crossed borders, with China confirming infection in its northwestern regions and reporting thousands of cattle affected. Without public acknowledgment, vaccination programs remain stalled in more than half of the regions, threatening devastating economic losses for farmers. China has begun culling and disinfection; Russia faces international criticism over management and the economic and social impact on its farmers.

articleSummary: Undercover investigators in Hanoi posed as traders to dismantle a ring trafficking diseased pigs to markets. For about 30 nights since the Lunar New Year 2026, they infiltrated the Van Phuc slaughterhouse complex in Thanh Tri, revealing a system that mixed healthy and sick pigs and moved them to markets and school-meal suppliers. Key figures include Nguyen Thi Hien, owner of slaughterhouse B6, accused of slaughtering sick pigs alongside healthy stock for profit; Do Van Thanh from Vinh Phuc, who sourced diseased pigs from Vinh Phuc and old Tuyen Quang without proper certification and used fake contracts plus a Phu Tho veterinary officer to obtain a “sanitary certificate” to enter Van Phuc; and Hiien who slaughtered pigs for hire at 100,000 VND each. On March 16–17, authorities seized about 30 tons of pigs, with 68 pigs entering the Hiền’s station (11 alive, 17 slaughtered; rest sold). Lab tests found 244 kg ASF-positive in Van Phuc consignments and 167 kg ASF-positive in Cuong Phát shipments. Since early 2026, ~3,600 diseased or mixed pigs (~300 tons) have been moved to markets. Several officials face charges for food-safety violations and veterinary fraud; investigations continue into related school-meal links. 24/7 veterinary control teams operate at Van Phuc.

articleSummary: Imported measles continues to threaten Brazil’s elimination status: 38 cases in 2025 and 2 in 2026, all imported. After a 2019 reintroduction, Brazil’s elimination certificate (2016) was revoked; vaccination coverage remains below the 95% two-dose MMR target, despite gains during the Covid-19 pandemic. PAHO reports 15,922 measles cases in the Americas from 2025 to the second week of 2026, mostly in the United States, Mexico and Canada—hosts of the 2026 World Cup, with an estimated 7 million visitors including thousands of Brazilians; Bolivia is the origin of the recent Brazilian cases. To avert outbreaks and potential loss of measles-free status, Brazil emphasizes three pillars: higher vaccination (including adults with irregular schemas), enhanced surveillance, and rapid outbreak response. Campos Lindos, Tocantins, demonstrated effective contact tracing and ring vaccination; SUS provides free MMR in two doses for children 12 months+, and one dose for adults 30–59.

articleSummary: Rabies remains a preventable yet deadly infection; vaccination, prompt wound care, and timely post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) can stop transmission.
